T: If we're kind and polite, the world will be right. And there will be sandwiches.
D: Paddington is wrongly sent to prison and wins over the inmates with his marmalade.
P: Serve the sandwiches when Paddington teaches Knuckles to make marmalade.
S: Bread buttered thick, spread with homemade marmalade (Seville oranges simmered whole an hour, shredded, boiled with sugar to 105C), cut into triangles.
the pop-up book of London he wants for Aunt Lucy

Vanilla butter biscuits cut into Big Ben, buses and Tower Bridge shapes, baked golden and piped with red, white and blue royal icing. Beat 125g soft butter with 100g caster sugar and 1 egg, then mix in 250g plain flour and 1 tsp vanilla. Chill 30 minutes, roll to 4mm and cut into London landmark shapes. Bake at 170C for 10 minutes and cool. Beat 1 egg white with 250g icing sugar and a squeeze of lemon until stiff, divide and colour red and blue, and pipe details.
Paddington's disastrous day at the barber shop
Self-raising flour with cold butter rubbed in, milk mixed in lightly, patted out, cut into fingers, glazed with milk, baked at 220C for 12 minutes. Jam and clotted cream.
M: Prison canteen chicken and leek pie
the grim canteen he turns into something lovely

Chicken thigh, leek and mushroom in a creamy thyme and mustard sauce under a flaky puff pastry lid, baked golden, with buttered peas. Cook 800g diced chicken thighs in 40g butter until browned, then add 2 sliced leeks and 250g sliced mushrooms and soften. Stir in 2 tbsp flour, then 250ml chicken stock, 200ml cream, 1 tsp Dijon and thyme and simmer until thick. Cool, tip into a pie dish, top with puff pastry and brush with egg. Bake at 200C for 30 minutes. Serve with 300g buttered peas.

Thick pork sausages grilled slowly until sticky and browned, piled into soft white rolls with sweet buttery onions and English mustard or tomato sauce. Cook 3 sliced onions in 40g butter with a pinch of brown sugar over low heat for 25 minutes until soft and golden. Grill 8 thick pork sausages over medium heat for 15 minutes, turning often, until browned all over. Split 8 soft white rolls, add a sausage and a heap of onions, and serve with English mustard and tomato sauce.
W: the prison uniforms that come out of the wash pink
Butter, sugar, eggs and flour weighed equal, beaten light, baked in two tins at 180C for 22 minutes, filled with raspberry jam and whipped cream, topped with pale pink icing.
K: tea for the whole cell block

Strong English breakfast tea stirred with orange marmalade and lemon while hot, chilled, then poured over ice with orange slices and a splash of soda. Brew 5 tea bags in 1.2L boiling water for 4 minutes and remove. Stir in 4 tbsp orange marmalade and the juice of a lemon until dissolved, then chill. Fill four tall glasses with ice and orange slices, pour in the tea and top each with a splash of soda water.

s.how: Simmer 500g Seville oranges whole in 1.2L water for 1 hour, halve, scoop out the pips and shred the peel. Return to the liquid with 1kg sugar and the juice of 1 lemon and boil hard to 105C, then jar and cool. Butter 8 slices white bread thickly, spread with marmalade and cut into triangles.

s.how: Rub 60g cold butter into 350g self-raising flour, mix in 250ml milk lightly, pat out and cut into fingers. Glaze with milk and bake at 220C for 12 minutes. Serve with strawberry jam and clotted cream.
